sources.entry: C: _Compiling a Lisp_ (Lisp compiler to x86-64 machine code)

summary.title: Compiling a Lisp: Overture
summary.one_liner: Introduces a series that builds a small Lisp compiler in C that emits x86-64 machine code directly, adapted from Ghuloum's incremental compiler paper.
keywords: an incremental approach to compiler construction
takeaways: The series adapts Ghuloum's Scheme compiler paper into C and generates x86-64 machine code directly rather than text assembly.
Generating machine code directly makes in-process testing easier and avoids depending on an external assembler.
The series is planned as installments, each adding a feature such as integers, primitives, let, if, cons, procedure calls, and closures.
Recommended background includes C, some assembly, ASTs, and recursive tree traversal.
summary.summary: This is the opening post of a multi-part series by Bernstein on writing a Lisp compiler in C that outputs x86-64 machine code directly. It explains that the work adapts Abdulaziz Ghuloum's paper "An Incremental Approach to Compiler Construction" with differences in language and code generation. The author justifies the choices: C for learning by writing code yourself, direct machine code for testability and understanding instruction encoding, and Lisp for its small dynamically typed core. It ends with a planned feature roadmap, a list of series installments, and links to other Ghuloum-style implementations.
